title: Optimize preflight and follow-ups (solo notes)
content:
Context / purpose:
- Quick solo prep before the weekly Optimize / evals sync. Primary aim: triage the small but persistent QA regression observed on the A/B for short-chat reranking (A: baseline, B: prefix-cached + int8 quant). Need an actionable list to present and to move to owners after the call.

High-level summary (one-liner):
- B shows 1.9% drop in rerank P@3 on short-chat prompts for top-100 customers; latency improved 12% and per-token cost down ~18%. Suspect cache-invalidation + tokenization edge-case in the new prefix-caching layer for sequences < 24 tokens.

Quick numbers to surface in sync (grab from dashboards before meeting):
- Eval set: opt-short-chat-2026-07 (n=3,200 queries).
- Baseline P@3: 0.842. Variant B P@3: 0.825 (delta -0.017).
- Latency p95: Baseline 190ms -> B 168ms.
- KV cache hit rate (in B): 62% overall, but 34% for queries length <= 24 tokens.
- Tokenization mismatch counts (heuristic): 178 instances where normalization removed trailing punctuation in B flow.

Top hypotheses (ranked):
1) Prefix-caching incorrectly normalizes or trims short queries before computing cache key (most likely).
2) Quantization path (int8) slightly alters logits for short sequences leading to re-rank score drift (less likely given magnitude).
3) Rollout routing: ~12% of B traffic routed to an older model variant accidentally (config drift) leading to mixed signals in metric aggregation.

Preflight checklist (things I will verify just before presenting):
- [ ] Confirm latest dashboard run time and that metrics are computed on the same eval snapshot (avoid stale aggregation).
- [ ] Quick grep through prefix-caching changeset for any string normalization calls affecting token boundaries. (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/optimize/pull/314)
- [ ] Query KV cache logs for top-customer examples where hit rate was low; copy 5 representative short prompts to show in meeting.
- [ ] Re-run a 200-query sample locally with and without int8 to reproduce delta.
- [ ] Check rollout config (console route rules) for B to ensure we didn't route to legacy model. (linked Jira: OPT-879)

Examples to bring (copy-paste-able):
- "schedule standup?"  -> baseline top candidate: "Create a calendar event for standup"; B top candidate: "Open calendar and view events" (illustrative of subtle wording shift).
- "price of subscription" -> baseline ranks more feature-specific snippet first; B favors generic pricing blurb.

Meeting agenda (5-10 min total):
1) 60s TL;DR of numbers and impact on customers (show p95/pps + cost delta).
2) 2 min: show 2 concrete example failures (short prompts).
3) 2 min: present top hypotheses + evidence (cache hit breakdown, tokenization mismatch counts).
4) 2 min: propose immediate mitigations and next steps (rollback criteria, narrow canary, debug logging).
5) 1 min: assign owners and deadlines.

Immediate mitigations I'm proposing in the sync:
- Short-term: rollback prefix-caching for model-route X for customers flagged as high-sensitivity if we see >1.5% drop (automated cutoff).
- Short-term alt: force bypass cache for queries length <= 24 tokens in B to test hypothesis without full rollback.
- Medium-term: add normalized-to-raw mapping in cache-key computation and a unit test covering punctuation/whitespace normalization.
- Obs: Add a daily eval gate that compares P@3 on short-chat shard and alerts on >1% drop (link to alert runbook).

Open questions to ask during the sync:
- Is there appetite for a targeted canary (10% of traffic) that forces cache-bypass for <24 token queries?
- Do we prefer a fast rollback or a patch to key computation as initial remediation?
- Any known differences in tokenizers across model versions still live in the fleet?

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Kenji: collect 5 canonical failing queries and push to meeting thread (today EOD).
- Priya Shah: double-check rollout policy for B and confirm no cross-routing (by 2026-08-12 AM).
- Noah Kim: run int8 vs fp16 200-query local diff and attach diff file to OPT-879 (by 2026-08-12 EOD).
- Eng-oncall (TBD): prepare rollback plan for prefix-caching route (if OT >1.5% drop) -- create runbook snippet (by 2026-08-13).
- Product/PM: confirm customer impact priority for top-100 customers list (requested to PM triage).

Notes to self (quick):
- When showing examples, keep them anonymized (no PII). Use synthetic prompt variants if needed.
- Avoid heavy technical deep-dive unless SRE asks for it; prioritize clear next steps.
- If the team leans toward patch, push for a short visibility window with increased logging and a metric that tracks tokenization-mismatch rate.

Follow-ups after sync (I will do):
- Open a small debug job to sample cache keys from production for short queries (link results to OPT-879).
- Draft a test case for the tokenization-normalization unit test and add to PR #314.
- If approved, coordinate a 10% canary that bypasses caching for <24 tokens and schedule a 48h observation window.

Helpful snippets/commands to run locally during debug:
- curl to evaluation endpoint with --header "X-Experiment: opt-prefix-v2" --sample-file short-queries.json
- python scripts/compare_rankings.py --base baseline-output.json --cand b-output.json --metrics p_at_1 p_at_3 mrr

Misc / thoughts:
- This regression highlights how small infra optimizations (cache keys) can disproportionately affect short-turn dialogues — worth a short infra postmortem if root cause is normalization.
- Consider adding a short-chat optimization profile to Optimize that explicitly keys on token-count buckets so future changes are tested against these shards automatically.

End of notes. Will tidy and paste top sections to the meeting doc before sync.
